the lung injury induced by endotoxemia (lipopolysaccaride‐LPS) in BALB/c mice is not mediated by tumour necrosis factortNF) or neutrophils (polymorphonuclear leukocytes, PMN), but by reactive oxygen intermediates.

the role of TNF and reactive oxygen intermediaries in endotoxin‐induced lung oedema.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNF and PMN are not involved in LPS‐induc ed lung oedema.
TNF and PMN are not involved in the pathogenesis, at least in the early stages, of LPS‐induc‐ed oedema and mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LPS‐induces pulmonary oedema by a direct effect of endotoxin on endothelial cells, and this effect is mediated by reactive oxygen intermediates and is independent of TNF.

(i): TNF is not implicated in the pathogenesis and development of pulmonary oedemas; (ii) TNF is not the main mediator of lethality induced by LPS; (iii) reactive oxygen intermediates play a major role in LPS‐inducible pulmonary oedema; and (iv) PMN do not participate in the pathogenesis or in the development of pulmonary oedomas induced by LPS.
TNF and PMN play a minor role in the pulmonary oedema caused by LPS in mice, and that reactive oxygen intermedi‐ates are implicated in the pathogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TNF is not the only factor implicated in LPS‐induce lung oedema and that reactive oxygen intermediaties play a role.
TNF is not the main mediator in the pathogenesis induced by LPS in mice.
TNF is a key mediator of LPS lethality and that the production of reactive oxygen intermediates is necessary for the development of pulmonary oedemas.
